narrative:
On September 17, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 41.5%, hearing 1,289 of the 3,104 scheduled matters across 50 judges. This reflects an improvement compared to 35.8% (1,027 of 2,871) recorded on September 15 and 38.6% on September 10, though it trails the 50.8% efficiency mark achieved on September 11.

Substantial variation marked judge-level throughput. High clearance volumes were driven by S. Vishwajith Shetty in Court Hall 21, who took up 83 of 108 matters (76.9%), C.M. Poonacha in Hall 31, hearing 76 of 107 cases (71.0%), and G. Basavaraja in Hall 32, resolving 70 of 104 listings (67.3%). Anant Ramanath Hegde also demonstrated strong progress, hearing 84.0% of a 75-case cause list. In contrast, several dockets saw minimal movement due to heavy over-listing; B.M. Shyam Prasad heard only 1 of 279 matters on a single expanded list, Sachin Shankar Magadum left a 59-case roster entirely unaddressed, and K.V. Aravind heard none of the 85 scheduled matters in Hall 34.

Procedural stage analysis indicates that early-stage matters progressed most reliably. Admission matters converted at 53.2% (442 heard of 831), Orders reached 48.2% (441 of 914), and Preliminary Hearings achieved 48.1% (164 of 341). Dispositions slowed severely deeper in the pipeline: Final Hearings converted at just 23.6% (127 of 538), while Further Hearing matters stalled at 6.2% (20 of 324). 

By subject matter, Writ Petitions dominated the docket with 1,279 listings but registered a modest 34.3% hearing rate, slightly improving upon the 28.9% observed on September 15. Criminal matters moved substantially faster, led by Criminal Petitions at 53.9% (234 of 434) and Criminal Appeals at 64.8% (83 of 128), while Civil Revision Petitions led specialized categories at an 80.0% clearance rate.
